title: Dragonblight
body: The Dragonblight is the great white valley at the heart of southern Northrend, where dragons come when they are ready to die. Their bones lie across it in their thousands, and at its center rises Wyrmrest Temple, where the dragonflights meet under Alexstrasza. That peace is broken: Malygos's blue flight tears at the ley lines, the Scourge raises frost wyrms from the old bones, and in the north Angrathar the Wrathgate bars the way into Icecrown, while Naxxramas hangs over Wintergarde in the east.

title: Agmar's Hammer
body: Agmar's Hammer, a fortress of black, jagged metal in the west of the Dragonblight, is the Horde's testament to its power here, and Overlord Agmar rules it from his throne in Hellscream's name, reading every letter before it leaves. Taunka refugees shelter at Westwind on the road from the tundra, an image of a Sunreaver archmage speaks for the Kirin Tor, and the unbound death knight Koltira Deathweaver has taken up residence for a time.

parts.body: A flesh-bound tome in the Scourge's tongue, which only Koltira could read, named members of the Cult of the Damned across the continent, among them orcs the hold's traitor-hunter had known for years.

title: Stars' Rest
body: Stars' Rest is the Alliance's outpost in the west of the Dragonblight, held by night elves around a moonwell from which the liquid fire of Elune is drawn to cleanse the beasts the Scourge has tainted. An image of a Kirin Tor archmage watches the blue dragonflight's work in the west, and east of the camp the ancients of the Lothalor Woodlands are being corrupted by the magic loosed across the land.

parts.body: A wounded courier reached the camp with a list of traitors in the Alliance's ranks, ambushed by Anub'ar who had known he was coming.

title: Moonrest Gardens
body: Moonrest Gardens, in the far west, was the resting place of a noble company of Highborne elves, and it lay on a ley line nexus. The blue dragonflight's mage hunters came with a giant device that now floats above the ruins, the Surge Needle, and bored a great pit into the gardens, and the morning they did, the land of the western Dragonblight shook and tore apart. The ghosts of the Highborne rose and slew half the mage hunters.

parts.body: The blue flight used the needle to destroy the nexus and redirect its power at will, and its plans showed it seeking an accord with the Ethereum.
sources: quest 12000 and 11999 descriptions (resting place of Highborne; ley line nexus; surge needle; the ghosts decimated half the mage hunters)

parts.body: The stolen power was carried beneath the land to the Azure Dragonshrine, where it emboldened the blues to attack Wyrmrest itself.

title: Moa'ki Harbor
body: Moa'ki Harbor is the home of the Dragonblight Kalu'ak, whose turtle riders carry travelers to their kin at Unu'pe and Kamagua. A great upheaval has just torn the land, and the village of Indu'le on the bluffs above its lake has gone silent: its ghosts walk the huts, its survivors wander out of their minds, and a stone elder still stands in its northwest corner.

parts.body: The stone elder told what happened: the elves' sacred ground to the west was torn asunder, and its magic came up through the lake and killed most of the village in an instant.

parts.body: The sea goddess Oacha'noa answered the harbor's mystic: the Kalu'ak must stand with the outsiders, for if the blue dragons win control of the world's magic, all are doomed.

title: Wyrmrest Temple
body: Wyrmrest Temple, said to have been raised by the titans, stands at the center of the Dragonblight, and here the dragonflights confer in peace amid the bones of their ancestors. Alexstrasza holds court at its summit with her consort Krasus, beside ambassadors of the green, bronze and even black flights; the black one sneers at all of them. The peace has been broken: the blue dragonflight has launched a surprise attack on the temple itself.

parts.body: Beneath the temple lies the Ruby Sanctum of the red dragonflight. Its entry lies in ruins and its guardians have been violently slain, and Krasus fears the worst.

title: Alexstrasza the Life-Binder
body: Alexstrasza the Life-Binder, Aspect of the red dragonflight, is the Queen of the Dragons, and from the summit of Wyrmrest she leads the Wyrmrest Accord. She greets mortals as friends she has known since before they were born, and she abhors the loss of any life, yet her flight is at war on every side: Malygos has turned the blues against the world's magic and against the temple, and the Scourge defiles the shrines and bones of her kind.

parts.body: The blue flight dares to attack the temple because it uses enormous amounts of the very magic it calls a threat to Azeroth. If Malygos will not see sense, the Accord must act.
sources: creature_template 26917 (Queen of the Dragons)

parts.body: North of the temple the Scourge digs at the bones of Galakrond, progenitor of dragonkind, from whom the titans created the Aspects; should it raise him, all the armies at the Wrathgate have done would be for naught.

title: Galakrond's Rest
body: North of Wyrmrest lie the dying grounds of Galakrond, the progenitor of dragonkind, whose bones are larger than all the Aspects together. The Scourge is digging them up. Scavengers labor in the snow, rotting storm giants and frost wyrms guard the digs, and from the ridge above a grand necrolord riding a rebuilt storm giant shouts that the Lich King demands more frost wyrms for Angrathar, and soon the bones of Galakrond will rise.

title: Angrathar the Wrathgate
body: Angrathar the Wrathgate is the barred entrance to Icecrown, a vast gate in the mountains at the northern edge of the Dragonblight, its metal pulsing as if alive. Before it the Alliance and the Horde fight side by side: Highlord Bolvar Fordragon commands from Fordragon Hold, and Saurfang the Younger leads the Kor'kron Vanguard in his father's battle armor. The Scourge pours out to meet them, and frost wyrms strafe the field.

parts.body: The elder Saurfang sent his son to command here, his heart and strength where he could not be, fearing young Hellscream's victories were leading the Horde back toward a dark place.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Dragonblight (the barred entrance to Icecrown)

parts.body: The strange ore of the Wintergarde Mine is exactly what the Wrathgate is made of, and the Highlord means to find its weakness.

parts.body: Since the battle the field has fallen strangely still. The dead of all sides lie where they fell, the camps wait without their commanders, and Alexstrasza has come down to look over what remains.

title: Wintergarde
body: Wintergarde Keep holds the eastern border of the Dragonblight, the 7th Legion's fortress, and above it hangs the necropolis Naxxramas, sent down by the Lich King after the Alliance struck at the Wrathgate. The village below the keep is gone: its ruins are the Carrion Fields, a breeding ground of the Scourge, where the dead rise from the crypt and the mine has been lost. High Commander Halford Wyrmbane means to rebuild under the necropolis's shadow.

parts.body: A demo-gnome sent into the lost mine overheard that the Scourge calls its strange ore saronite, and speaks the name Yogg-Saron with great contempt.
sources: quest 12235 description (Naxxramas sent down upon us; the lower village lost)

parts.body: The Scourge's ground commander, Thel'zan the Duskbringer, was once Father Inigo Montoy, a cleric of the Argent Dawn who became what he hated most.

title: New Hearthglen
body: On the cliffs of the southern coast the Scarlet Onslaught has built a new Hearthglen, with walls, barracks, an abbey and ballistae, its streets full of footmen and raven priests and its cages full of Forsaken prisoners. High General Abbendis commands, with an admiral of the Scarlet Fleet named Barean Westwind close at hand, and her soldiers carry copies of The Path of Redemption, said to hold her prophetic ramblings.

parts.body: Her journal tells how it began: a voice came to her in dreams, whispering 'Come to me', and she knew it for the Light, though her breath misted in the warm sun as it spoke.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Dragonblight (Scarlet Onslaught at New Hearthglen)

parts.body: Westwind, who by all accounts had died on these shores an age ago, appeared at her door far too young, and since then the Light has fallen silent.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Dragonblight (Scarlet Onslaught at New Hearthglen)

parts.body: When Abbendis fell, Westwind told her she had served her purpose, promised her killers a meeting in Icecrown and was gone.

title: Venomspite
body: Venomspite is the Forsaken town in the east of the Dragonblight, where Vengeance Pass leads north to the Carrion Fields. Its high executor has decreed death for every member of the Scarlet Onslaught to the south, and its chief plaguebringer promises to ravage the living, or rather, he corrects himself, the Scourge. The perfected blight of New Agamand came here to be made safe to handle.

parts.body: The Forsaken's blight did nothing to a captured Onslaught soldier: a prayer from a grand admiral named Westwind protects them.

title: The Forgotten Shore
body: On the southeastern coast the Forgotten Shore is strewn with broken ships whose crews never left. Ghostly soldiers of the Alliance walk the beach, not knowing they are dead, crying out against a betrayal and a prince who gave them his word, while the Argent Crusade camps nearby at Dawn's Reach.

parts.body: The ghosts think Arthas a hero, yet it was he who ordered their ships burned and left them to die in this frozen land, as an old Argent who sailed in the prince's fleet as a lad remembers.
sources: quest 12290 description (spirits of the damned, once brave soldiers of the Alliance, bound to this world)

parts.body: In a cave near Scarlet Point the past showed Arthas taking up Frostmourne against Muradin Bronzebeard's warnings, and Muradin struck down, waking with no memory of who he was. He might yet live.
